name: Teleport Pair
description: Two pads wired as one passage: step on A, arrive at B. It owns the pairing, the transit cooldown, and the exit offset, because the three failure modes of teleporters — arriving inside geometry, bouncing endlessly between pads, and landing with no idea which way you face — are all solved here and nowhere else. Velocity handling is an explicit choice rather than an accident: preserving momentum makes the pair a traversal tool (launch in, fly out), while zeroing it makes the pair a reset, and a puzzle designer needs both. This component deliberately does not own why the pair exists — routing and gating belong to the level and to world.ability_gate — and it does not reposition bodies by itself; the actual move is movement.character_body's, since only the body can teleport without desyncing its own collision state.

inputs.name: pairId
inputs.description: Identifier linking the two ends. More than one pair can coexist in a level; the id, not position, defines who connects to whom.

inputs.name: bidirectional
inputs.description: False makes A→B one-way. One-way pairs create commitment puzzles — drop in and find another way out; bidirectional pairs are shortcuts.

inputs.name: preserveVelocity
inputs.description: True carries momentum through the transit, enabling portal-style fling puzzles. False zeroes it, which is the readable default for compact puzzle rooms.

inputs.name: cooldownSeconds
inputs.description: Per-entity dead time after arriving before that entity can transit again. Without it, landing on the exit pad teleports you straight back — forever.

inputs.name: exitOffset
inputs.description: Arrival position relative to the destination pad, chosen so the rider lands beside the pad trigger, not on top of it.
